title: Distributed Key-Value Store
intro: Master the design of a globally distributed, fault-tolerant key-value store modeled on Amazon's foundational Dynamo paper.
objectives: Implement consistent hashing with virtual nodes for uniform data distribution.
Formulate quorum read/write equations ($R + W > N$) for tunable consistency.
Resolve concurrent write conflicts using Vector Clocks and Read Repair.
body:
### The Dynamo Architecture Playbook
A distributed key-value store provides two simple operations: `get(key)` and `put(key, value)`, but scales across thousands of nodes worldwide:
- **Partitioning**: Consistent Hashing Ring with virtual nodes (vnodes) to prevent hot-spot skew.
- **Replication**: The coordinator node replicates keys to the $N$ successive physical nodes clockwise on the ring.
- **Tunable Quorum**: Configure replica count $N$, read quorum $R$, and write quorum $W$. When $R + W > N$, the read quorum is mathematically guaranteed to overlap with the write quorum by at least one node, providing strong consistency.
- **Sloppy Quorum & Hinted Handoff**: If designated replica nodes are temporarily unreachable during network partitioning, healthy peer nodes temporarily accept writes and hand them back once the primary recovers.
keyIdea: Tunable quorums ($R + W > N$) allow engineers to dynamically dial between sub-millisecond write latency ($W=1$) and strict read consistency ($R+W>N$).

concepts.title: Read Repair
concepts.body: When a client reads from $R$ nodes and detects conflicting version timestamps, the coordinator immediately writes the latest version back to the stale nodes in the background.

concepts.title: Anti-Entropy with Merkle Trees
concepts.body: Nodes compare cryptographic hash trees of their key ranges to synchronize missing data with minimal network payload transfer.

examples: Amazon DynamoDB and Apache Cassandra distributed storage engines.

resources.title: Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store

quiz.prompt: In a distributed key-value store with replication factor N=3, what values of R (read quorum) and W (write quorum) guarantee strong consistency?
quiz.explanation: When R=2 and W=2, R + W = 4 > 3 (N), guaranteeing that the read set intersects with at least one node from the write set.
